image_description:
## 1. Chart type
- **Faceted small-multiple line/trajectory chart** with stylized closed-loop paths in each panel.
- Each panel shows one highlighted loop plus several thinner background loops.

## 2. Layout techniques
- **Small multiples / faceting**: 8 separate panels arranged in a grid.
- **Color encoding** across panels: panel highlight colors follow a magenta-to-blue scale tied to the “Hits are different” → “Hits are similar” legend.
- No visible stacking.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Song title | Categorical/nominal | Text label above each panel |
| Artist | Categorical/nominal | Text label above each panel |
| Year | Temporal | Large text label inside each panel |
| Similarity / difference of hits | Ordinal (shown as a continuum) | Color/hue of highlighted loop; legend gradient from magenta to blue |
| Individual song/example | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate panels |
| Path/trajectory shape values | Quantitative | 2D position forming the loop/path within each panel |
| Reference/background trajectories | Quantitative | Thin line paths in the background within each panel |
| Top marker position | Quantitative | Position of black square and short vertical line near top of each loop |

comments.raw_comment: Displayed in the graph are eight sonic “fingerprints” of the Top 10 summer hits for 1998-2018. I notice that for each year displayed, there are several thin shapes, with a thick outlined circle on top. I infer that these several thinner circles refer to other hits of that particular summer, or perhaps even year. I see how for the somewhat circle-shaped “fingerprints,” those colored hot pink have several thin circles underneath them moving in several different directions, while those colored blue have several thin circles underneath them that tend to overlap and resemble each other. This pattern makes sense, because hot pink indicates the hits of that year or summer are different, and thus have different acoustics, danceability, energy, and/or valence. Likewise, this trend make sense also for the blue circles, as blue indicates the hits are similar, and thus the shape of the thin blue circles are generally the same. Among each fingerprint, I notice that danceability is a consistently prominent factor in determining whether or not a song becomes a top hit. I wonder, has this always been the case? Why or why not?
